title: No network/proxy/TLS guidance for enterprise deployments; Requirements omit the updater hosts
evidence:
README.md Requirements: "Outbound network access (at runtime) to `login.microsoftonline.com`, `graph.microsoft.com`, and — only when you use those features — `*.vault.azure.net` ..., `outlook.office365.com` ..., `management.azure.com` ..., and `api.loganalytics.azure.com`" — github.com is not listed, yet apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:47-48 `"endpoints": ["https://github.com/tiredithumans/azapptoolkit/releases/latest/download/latest.json"]` (asset downloads redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`).
`grep -n -i 'proxy|firewall|allowlist|TLS inspection|certificate store' README.md docs/DEVELOPMENT.md docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md` → no matches.

What the binary actually does (undocumented): reqwest 0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:310 `auto_sys_proxy: true,` and :417-418 `if config.auto_sys_proxy { proxies.push(ProxyMatcher::system()); }`; hyper-util 0.1.21 matcher.rs:101-102 "This checks the same environment variables as `from_env()`, and if not set, checks the system configuration for values for the OS", :704-718 reads Windows `ProxyEnable`/`ProxyServer`/`ProxyOverride` (no `AutoConfigURL`/PAC handling in the file); Cargo.lock hyper-util deps include `system-configuration` and `windows-registry`. TLS roots come from the OS store: Cargo.lock:3937 reqwest → `rustls-platform-verifier`. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:188 already classifies "NOT Entra: a TLS-intercepting proxy, WAF or captive portal".
rationale: The README targets MDM/Group Policy rollouts (MSI section, `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` for "MDM/Group Policy deployments") — exactly the environments with egress allowlists, explicit proxies and TLS inspection. Today an admin cannot learn from the docs that (a) auto-update needs github.com/objects.githubusercontent.com, (b) `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and the OS static proxy are honoured but PAC/WPAD is not, (c) TLS inspection works only if the inspecting CA is in the OS trust store, or (d) what the "a proxy answered" sign-in error means.
proposal: Add a "Network requirements" subsection under Requirements: the full host allowlist per feature plus the two updater hosts; a "Behind a proxy" note (env vars, OS static proxy, no PAC, how `NO_PROXY` interacts with the 127.0.0.1 loopback redirect); a "TLS inspection" note (OS trust store via rustls-platform-verifier; certificate pinning is not used); and a troubleshooting bullet for the text/html-from-login-host error. Sovereign clouds: list the per-cloud hosts already in the CSP (tauri.conf.json:25).
verifier_notes: Verified: README.md:292-298 host list omits github.com although apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:47-48 sets the updater endpoint to github.com/.../latest.json (asset downloads redirect to objects.githubusercontent.com); grep for proxy/firewall/allowlist/TLS inspection across README, DEVELOPMENT.md and OPERATOR-ROLES.md returns nothing. Behaviour claims check out against the vendored sources: reqwest-0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:310 `auto_sys_proxy: true` and :417 pushes ProxyMatcher::system(); hyper-util-0.1.21 matcher.rs:704-708 reads ProxyEnable/ProxyServer only (no AutoConfigURL/PAC); Cargo.lock reqwest depends on rustls-platform-verifier (OS trust store); crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:183-192 already classifies the TLS-intercepting-proxy case. The README's MSI/Intune/Group-Policy audience makes medium fair. One overstatement to drop: the NO_PROXY/127.0.0.1 loopback note is moot — the loopback redirect is an inbound browser→listener hop, not an outbound reqwest call; the proxy guidance should cover the Microsoft and GitHub hosts only.

title: Exchange mailbox-scoping unavailability (no Exchange client, or breaker tripped) is invisible in the run result, the workbench and every export
rationale: By design a non-Exchange-admin gets org-wide weight for every mail permission (never under-report), and that trade-off should stay. But the consequence for the operator is that apps already scoped via RBAC are listed as Critical 'Org-wide mailbox access' with a 'Scope…' Fix that will fail, the healthy 'Mailbox access scoped' group is empty, and the run is cached and exported as complete. `coverage_sentences` (audit.rs:636-642) already adds a caveat when the sign-in report was unavailable; the analogous, higher-impact caveat for mailbox scoping does not exist, and `AuditRunResult` carries no field for it. Nothing in web-rs/views/audit_view or security_view mentions Exchange availability (grep).
proposal: Add `mailbox_scoping_resolved: bool` (`#[serde(default = true)]`-style) to `AuditRunResult`, `AuditExportCoverage` and `CachedAuditRun`, set false when `exo` is `None` or `exo_tripped` is set at the end of the run; add a sentence in `coverage_sentences` ('Mailbox scoping could not be resolved — org-wide mailbox findings may include applications already confined via Exchange RBAC; sign in as an Exchange Administrator to refine') and a Callout in the Org-wide mailbox finding group. Keep it out of `degraded` so the run stays cacheable, matching the sign-in precedent.
verifier_notes: audit.rs:899-907 logs Exchange unavailability at `info!` and returns `None`; score_one flips `exo_tripped` at :1569 with another `info!`. Neither reaches `AuditRunResult` (dto/audit.rs:16-56: only `sign_in_report_available`/`sign_in_consent_required`/`truncated`/`degraded`), `AuditExportCoverage` (dto/audit.rs:92-102) or `coverage_sentences` (audit.rs:613-651, which does carry the sign-in caveat at :636-642). The frontend never mentions Exchange availability: audit_view/filter.rs:71-72 only acknowledges the degrade in a comment, and groups.rs:57/127 blurbs assume scoping was resolved. The degrade-to-org-wide scoring is a documented decision (audit-findings-and-remediation.md:22-25 'never under-reported'), but not surfacing it is not — and for a non-Exchange-admin the Critical 'Org-wide mailbox access' rows offer a Scope Fix that needs the same Exchange client and will fail. The proposal (a serde-defaulted flag on the run/cache/export plus a sentence and a Callout, kept out of `degraded` so caching is unchanged) mirrors the sign-in precedent exactly and is feasible.

title: Enterprise-app assignee/group read failures degrade to empty with no `skipped` record — manifest silently under-reports access
rationale: The whole-object skip is recorded, but a per-SP failure of `appRoleAssignedTo` or `memberOf` produces an `EnterpriseAppBackup` with zero assignees/groups and no marker. On restore the app gets no assignments re-applied and the report shows nothing amiss; users who had access in the source silently do not in the destination. The architecture doc describes the degrade, but the `skipped` mechanism was added precisely so 'degrade to empty' is never invisible; extending it here is the consistent completion of that fix, not a re-litigation.
proposal: When `assigned[i]` or `groups[i]` is `Err(e)`, push `SkippedObject::new("enterpriseAppAssignments" / "enterpriseAppGroups", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("... could not be read: {e}"))` alongside the (partial) entry. Update the `SkippedObject.kind` doc list and the arch doc sentence to say partial reads are recorded. The DR view already renders `skipped` generically. Effort S.
verifier_notes: Accurate. backup.rs:553-563 maps `Err(_)` on `assigned[i]`/`groups[i]` to `Vec::new()` and pushes no `SkippedObject`; only the whole-SP failure at :566-576 is recorded. The session latch IS honoured here (`note_graph_failures` on assigned/groups at :546-548), so the dead-session case aborts — the gap is limited to transient per-item failures producing an entry with zero assignees/groups and no marker, which the reviewer states correctly. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:111-112 documents the degrade but gives no rationale beyond it, and the `skipped` doc (dto/backup.rs:59-66) argues the opposite direction. The DR view renders `kind`/`reason` generically (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:299-326), so new kinds need only the `SkippedObject.kind` doc (dto/backup.rs:78) and the arch sentence updated. Medium is fair: silent under-reporting of access in a DR manifest, but bounded to transient failures.

title: Conditional Access view ignores workload-identity targeting (conditions.clientApplications)
rationale: Graph's `conditionalAccessConditionSet` also carries `clientApplications { includeServicePrincipals, excludeServicePrincipals, servicePrincipalFilter }` — workload-identity Conditional Access, which targets precisely the service principals this tool manages. The model omits it, so (a) a policy that blocks THIS app's SP is invisible if its `applications` condition names other resources, and (b) a workload-identity policy with the usual `applications.includeApplications=["All"]` is reported as "applies (all)" for every app in the tenant, whether or not its SP is the targeted client. For an app-registration/enterprise-app admin tool this is the most relevant CA dimension and it is currently mis-reported in both directions.
proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (includeServicePrincipals / excludeServicePrincipals / servicePrincipalFilter) to `CaConditions` in crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:614-617. Resolve the SP object id backend-side in `list_conditional_access_for_app` via the existing `get_service_principal_by_app_id` (the CA tab is mounted on the app-registration pane keyed only by appId — conditional_access_tab.rs:20-23, application_detail_pane.rs:257 — and the shared `ConditionalAccessPanel` takes only `app_id`), tolerating a missing SP by skipping the client-side check. In `applies_reason`, apply exclude-wins on `excludeServicePrincipals`, then require an SP match when `clientApplications` is present (`workloadIdentity` / `workloadIdentityAll` / `workloadIdentityFilter` codes) before falling back to the resource-side `applications` reasons. Extend the table tests, document the new codes on `ConditionalAccessPolicyDto.applies_reason`, and update the tab copy at conditional_access_tab.rs:58-60.
verifier_notes: Premise real: `CaConditions` (models.rs:614-617) has only `applications`; conditional_access.rs:53-58 returns None when `applications` is absent and `applies_reason` (:73-116) evaluates only resource-side includes. A repo-wide grep for workload/clientApplications finds nothing in the CA path or docs, so this is an unaddressed gap, not a documented decision. The two mis-reporting directions follow from the code: a workload-identity policy with `includeApplications=["All"]` yields "all" for every app, and one whose `applications` names other resources is invisible for the targeted SP. Overstated detail: 'pass the SP object id in (the detail pane has it)' — the tab lives on the app-registration pane which only has appId, so the resolution belongs in the backend. Medium is fair for a feature gap that mis-reports in both directions.

title: MailboxReachersResult.exchange_available can never reflect the realistic degraded mode (missing Exchange consent / 403), so the summary's partial-coverage caveat never fires
rationale: For a signed-in operator with a UPN, exchange_available is always true. When Exchange.Manage is unconsented or the caller lacks Exchange admin rights — the common degraded case — the AAP read fails, the Exchange SP-store candidate source is dropped at info level, and every RBAC layer is Indeterminate, yet the result and its CSV export carry no coverage flag beyond the per-row unknown count. The doc's promised caveat is unreachable in practice.
proposal: Best-effort pre-acquire with `state.ensure_exchange_token(&tenant_id).await` and set exchange_available=false (keeping exo=None) on failure; additionally add `exchange_sp_store_read: bool` (or fold into exchange_available) set from the list_service_principals outcome so the summary/export can say "Exchange-registered apps without an Entra grant could not be enumerated". Update the doc sentence to match.
verifier_notes: Verified: exchange_available = exchange_client(..).ok().is_some() (permission_tester.rs:496-497); exchange_client only checks tenant_context and username (exchange/mod.rs:90-107) and never touches a token — exchange_client_checked (:116-122) is the pre-acquiring variant. So for any signed-in operator with a UPN the flag is always true; a missing Exchange.Manage consent or an admin-API 403 surfaces only as an Err from get_application_access_policies (dropped to None at :500-508) and from list_service_principals (info-log at :511-518), silently removing the Exchange-SP-store candidate source. The frontend caveat (web-rs views/resource_access/mailboxes.rs:54-57) and the doc sentence (resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:64-66) are therefore unreachable in the realistic degraded case. Partial mitigation the finding under-weights: the per-row unknown count does render ' · N couldn't be confirmed (need Exchange admin rights)' (mailboxes.rs:49-52), so the operator gets a hint about RBAC verdicts — but nothing flags that Exchange-only principals were not enumerated at all, which is the real under-report. Medium is fair. Proposal is feasible: AppState::ensure_exchange_token exists (state.rs:661-664) and is the same pre-acquire exchange_client_checked uses; adding a bool to MailboxReachersResult (dto/permission_tester.rs:99-106) is an additive wire change the CSV coverage block should also carry.

title: `plan_restore` dry-run skips the schema check and omits enterprise/MI/skipped counts the restore will act on
rationale: The plan is what the operator confirms against. A too-new manifest passes the dry-run and is refused only after Confirm; the plan lists app-registration work only, though Passes 4-5 will also re-apply SP settings, role assignments, group memberships and MI role re-binds; and restoring into the SOURCE tenant (which duplicates the entire estate) is the one case that shows no note, because the note is gated on `tenant_changed`.
proposal: Call `check_manifest_schema` in `plan_restore` (surface as a blocker like `cloud_mismatch`). Extend `RestorePlan` (all `serde(default)`) with `enterprise_apps_to_reapply`, `enterprise_apps_manual`, `managed_identities_to_rebind`, `skipped_in_backup: usize`, and render them in `RestorePlanView`; render an explicit warning when `!tenant_changed` ("This manifest was taken from THIS tenant — restoring will create duplicates of every app"). Effort S-M.
verifier_notes: All three sub-claims hold. `plan_restore` (restore.rs:87-98) calls only `build_restore_plan`; `check_manifest_schema` is invoked solely in `restore_tenant` (:155). `RestorePlan` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:351-368) has no enterprise/MI/skipped fields, and `build_restore_plan` (:129-147) sums only app-registration fields. The only tenant note in the plan view is `<Show when=move || plan.tenant_changed>` (dr.rs:444); the confirm modal (dr.rs:414-415) says 'creates new app registrations' generically but nothing flags the same-tenant duplicate case. Two honest caveats that keep this at medium rather than higher: the schema gap fails closed (refused at Confirm, never partially applied), so it is UX not safety; and all `RestorePlan` fields are `serde(default)`-compatible so the extension is additive and wire-safe as proposed. The same-tenant warning is the most valuable piece.

title: SAML create silently drops a failed claims policy or notification-email step; the wizard shows an unqualified success
rationale: Degrading rather than failing is a documented decision, but the degradation is invisible: `SamlSsoSummary.claims_policy_id` is `None` on failure and nothing in the frontend reads it, so an operator who filled in the Attributes & claims step sees the same success screen as one who did not, and discovers the missing claims at the first federated sign-in. The same applies to notification emails (the "nobody is warned" column on the expiry board). `RotateCredentialResult.warnings` already establishes the pattern for exactly this situation.
proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub warnings: Vec<String>` to `SamlSsoSummary`; in `configure_saml` push a human message on each degraded step ("Custom claims were not applied: <err>; open the SSO tab → Save claims to retry" / "Notification emails were not saved: <err>"). Render a warn `Callout` in `components/sso_summary.rs` when non-empty, and add a fixture with a warning so the GUI test covers it.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. sso/mod.rs:240-244 and 254-267 log-and-continue on notification-email and claims-policy failures; `SamlSsoSummary` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:201-225) has no `warnings` field, and a grep of apps/desktop/web-rs/src for `claims_policy_id`/`claimsPolicyId` outside ipc_mock returns nothing — `components/sso_summary.rs` never mentions claims, warnings or a Callout. So an operator who filled in claims sees the same success screen whether or not the policy landed. Degrading is documented as deliberate (mod.rs:254-256) but the invisibility is not. `RotateCredentialResult.warnings` (dto/keyvault.rs:149) is the established precedent and `Callout` is a listed UI primitive. Medium is fair.

evidence:
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/sharepoint.rs:204  pub async fn list_selected_item_permissions(
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/sharepoint.rs:223  pub async fn remove_selected_item_permission(
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:216  commands::sharepoint::remove_selected_item_permission,
Only UI caller of the family: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/scope_wizard.rs:206  let r = sharepoint::grant_selected_item_access(
`grep -rn "list_selected_item_permissions\|remove_selected_item_permission" web-rs/src` outside bindings/ipc_mock/demo → nothing.
rationale: AGENTS.md calls sub-site Selected scopes "a SECOND, non-enumerable mechanism": once a folder/list grant is made through the wizard there is no screen that shows it or takes it back, so the only way to undo a grant made in this app is Graph Explorer/PowerShell. The list + revoke commands are already implemented, registered and typed.
proposal: Add a revoke path where the grant is verified: extend the permission tester's SharePoint result (or a 'Selected item permissions' section on the SharePoint panel) with a `list_selected_item_permissions` table for the resolved URL and a per-row Revoke calling `remove_selected_item_permission` behind a confirm, carrying the doc's caveat that an empty result means 'no grants on this resource', never 'no item-level access for this app'. Reuse `ItemSelectionPanel`'s URL resolution. Add a GUI shard test with mocked fixtures.
verifier_notes: Confirmed that `list_selected_item_permissions` and `remove_selected_item_permission` (bindings/sharepoint.rs:204, :223; registered lib.rs:216) have no UI caller — only `grant_selected_item_access` (scope_wizard.rs:206) and `resolve_sharepoint_resource` (item_selection_panel.rs:88) are used. Overstated on the 'never listed' half: the permission tester already answers 'does THIS app reach this library/folder/file' by URL — permission_tester_view.rs:207 accepts 'a SharePoint site, library, folder or file URL', `test_site_access` (commands/permission_tester.rs:1053-1070) resolves it and reads item permissions via `list_list_item_permissions` (:960), and CHANGELOG.md:80 says the 'Scoped (selected items)' badge now links there for exactly this. What is genuinely missing is (a) a per-resource view of ALL app grants and (b) any in-app revoke — a grant the wizard creates cannot be undone in the app. docs/architecture/sharepoint-selected.md:53 ('Any future panel must say so') anticipates a panel rather than ruling one out, so this is not a documented deliberate omission. Medium is fair for a create-without-delete asymmetry on a permission grant.

title: Bulk-delete confirmation says 'cannot be undone' although Entra soft-deletes for 30 days (single-app dialog already says so); no in-app 'Recently deleted' list or restore
rationale: TOP-5 #1. Entra soft-deletes application objects for 30 days (`GET /directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.application`, `POST /directory/deletedItems/{id}/restore`, `DELETE /directory/deletedItems/{id}` for permanent removal). The toolkit ships `delete_application` and `bulk_delete_applications` (the latter seeded by multi-select and 'Fix all N' flows) yet has no view of, or route back from, the recycle bin, and both the bulk bar and the CHANGELOG-described single-app dialog tell the operator the action is irreversible. That is the wrong message for the one moment an admin most needs the true one: after a mis-targeted bulk delete they will reach for PowerShell (`Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem`) — exactly what this app exists to replace — or assume the app is gone and recreate it, which mints a new appId and breaks every consumer. The read needs only `Directory.Read.All` (already the sign-in scope); restore/permanent-delete ride the existing `write` scope feature (`Application.ReadWrite.All`). Restoring also re-creates the SP link, so the existing `invalidate_app_lists` + pairing index refresh is the only cache work.
proposal: (1) S: reword only bulk_action_bar.rs:817 to match the single-app dialog's existing wording (restorable from the Entra recycle bin for 30 days). (2) M: as proposed — `commands/applications/deleted.rs` with list/restore/purge over `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.application` (paged with `$top`), registered in `generate_handler![]`, bindings, a 'Recently deleted' surface with restore, `invalidate_app_lists` on Ok, `demo::register_fixtures` entries, and an 'Undo (restore N)' action on the bulk-delete toast.
verifier_notes: Bulk copy is real: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/bulk_action_bar.rs:817 says 'Permanently delete ... This cannot be undone.' and `delete_application` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:403-411) is a plain DELETE /applications/{id}, which Entra soft-deletes. No `deletedItems` code exists anywhere (only docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:59 mentions soft-delete for MIs). BUT the single-app dialog is already correct: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_detail_pane.rs:269 body reads 'Deletion can be undone from the Entra admin center within 30 days.' — so 'both ... dialogs tell the operator the action is irreversible' is half wrong; only the bulk bar misinforms. The bulk completion toast (bulk_action_bar.rs:1187) has no undo path. Recycle-bin list/restore is a genuine absence.

title: Claims editor has no advisory validation for edits Graph rejects or that silently strip the default claims
evidence:
claims_editor.rs:329-334 (a row with only an attribute is emitted)
    let empty = entry.id.is_none()
        && entry.extension_id.is_none()
        && entry.value.is_none()
        && entry.saml_claim_type.is_none()
        && entry.jwt_claim_type.is_none();
    (!empty).then_some(entry)

crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:23-24
/// The emitted claim is named by `saml_claim_type` (SAML token claim URI) and/or
/// `jwt_claim_type` (JWT/OIDC token claim name); at least one is normally set.

claims_editor.rs:565 `<Input value=row.attribute placeholder="Transformation id" />` — never checked against `transforms` ids (671).
claims_editor.rs:459-461 — "Edit" pushes a new override row on every click (no dedupe by SamlClaimType).
claims_editor.rs:433-440 — `include_basic` checkbox with no warning when unchecked with an empty schema.
docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md:41-49 — UriListState's opt-in advisory validation is the precedent ("points at the offender before the round trip … but never gates Save").
rationale: The editor drops fully blank rows but forwards half-typed ones: a row with a source attribute and no SAML/JWT claim name, a transformation-sourced claim referencing a transformation id that does not exist, or two rows with the same SamlClaimType (two clicks on "Edit") all reach `set_claims_mapping`, which has already detached the old policy before Graph rejects the new one — leaving the app with NO claims policy. Unchecking "Include the basic claim set" with nothing else defined removes name/email/givenname/surname from every assertion with no warning, which is the dangerous edit the `is_empty()` doc calls "suppressing the basic set".
proposal: Add `ClaimsEditorState::problems(&self) -> Vec<String>` (reactive: reads the signals tracked) covering: row with neither SamlClaimType nor JwtClaimType; transformation source whose id matches no transform; duplicate SamlClaimType/JwtClaimType; `!include_basic && schema.is_empty()`; transform with no output claim. Render them in a `Callout tone="warn"` above the Save button in both hosts; advisory only. Additionally harden `set_claims_mapping` to create+assign the new policy BEFORE detaching the old one (Graph allows one assignment at a time, so detach → create is required, but validating the definition via a dry `create` first, then detach, then assign, avoids the no-policy end state). Unit-test `problems()`.
verifier_notes: schema_row_to_dto (claims_editor.rs:329-334) drops only fully-empty rows, so attribute-only rows, transformation rows pointing at non-existent ids (565), and duplicate SamlClaimType rows from repeated 'Edit' clicks (459-461, seed_basic_override always pushes) all reach set_claims_mapping, which detaches the old policy (sso/mod.rs:1643-1655) BEFORE apply_claims_policy (1657-1661) — a Graph rejection therefore leaves the SP with no policy. include_basic checkbox (433-440) has no warning; dto/sso.rs:116-119 and 144-149 describe unchecking it as suppressing the basic set. frontend-workspace.md:41-49 establishes advisory validation as the precedent. Reordering to create -> detach -> assign is feasible (a claimsMappingPolicy may exist unassigned); note it needs orphan cleanup if detach then fails.

                f::password_credential("crm-legacy-secret", "a1Z", f::date(2024, 2, 1)),

demo/mod.rs:164-172  f::date(2025, 9, 28), ... cred_status: S::Active,

As of 2026-09-26 every showcase secret (2025-08-30, 2025-07-09, 2025-09-28, 2024-02-01) and all seven filler secrets (2026-01-31) are expired, so the list says "Expiring"/"Active" and the tab says "Expired" for the same app. The SSO board shows an expiry of 2026-08-27 next to "15 days". title: On Linux without a Secret Service the sign-in hard-fails after the browser round trip; the requirement is undocumented and the `keyring` hint is misleading

The in-memory refresh-token fallback is a product/security decision for the team (access tokens are already memory-only, so a session-only mode is defensible), not an obvious fix; if adopted, surface a `keyring_unavailable` notice as proposed.

title: Audit never reads federated identity credentials, so a planted or over-broad OIDC trust is invisible in the security workbench
rationale: The codebase's own module doc explains why a FIC is the most dangerous credential to miss: no secret, no expiry, silently accepted by Graph even when wrong. The audit scores secrets and certificates (Rules 5-9, 17) and even flags 'Uses client secret(s)' as a hygiene nudge toward federation, yet it never looks at the federated credentials an app already has — so an attacker-planted trust (`iss` = a GitHub org the tenant does not own, or a `sub` matching every branch via a flexible FIC `claimsMatchingExpression`), or a FIC left behind after a repo was archived, produces a clean row. The batched per-app FIC read already exists for the backup path, so the audit can reuse it at the same fan-out cost class; the validation rules in `core::federation` give the classifier.
proposal: (M) In `run_audit`, fetch FICs per app through the backup's batched reader (only for apps that hold app permissions or admin-consented scopes, to bound cost), pass `federated: Vec<FederatedIdentityCredential>` into `score_application`, add advisory Rule 21: list issuers/subjects; flag `claimsMatchingExpression` present, issuers outside a per-tenant allowlist in `TenantDefaults` (e.g. `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` with an org prefix, the tenant's AKS OIDC issuer URL), and `sub` values without a ref/environment constraint. New `issue::FEDERATED_TRUST_REVIEW` marker + finding group (no one-click fix — admin-judged). CSV/JSON export columns. Table tests with the fixtures in `client/tests/credentials.rs`. Expected effect: the workbench sees the credential class its own docs call the worst case.
verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/federation.rs:1-19 documents why a FIC is a silently-accepted trust; the audit never reads FICs (grep federated in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs and core/audit = 0 hits; `score_application` takes only `&Application`, scoring.rs:871-876); backup already has `batch_list_federated_credentials` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/credentials.rs:86-91) and backup.rs:11-13 confirms FICs are captured; `validate_federated_credential` (federation.rs:36) gives a classifier; fixtures exist in crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/credentials.rs (:218+). No documented decision excludes FICs from scoring (docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md has no mention). Minor: rules stop at 18, so it would be Rule 19; the issuer allowlist in `TenantDefaults` must be added to the exhaustive `apply_tenant_defaults` destructure per AGENTS.md. Medium is fair for a security workbench blind to the credential class its own docs call the worst case.

title: `consent_required` is flattened to `token_error` inside every client call, so the shared UI consent fallback never fires for scoped calls; docs still blame a `String` boundary that no longer exists
rationale: `token_adapter::token_error` (token_adapter.rs:21-29) now carries `consent_required` across the boundary as `TokenError { code: "consent_required", .. }`, but `ui_code()` only passes the two re-auth-fatal codes through and collapses everything else to `token_error`. So a Graph write/sharepoint/policy call that hits a missing consent still reaches the UI as `token_error`, and `Session::report_consent_required` (web-rs/state/errors.rs:112-117, keyed on `e.code == "consent_required"`) — described in the doc as "one shared fallback" for commands with no bespoke button — cannot fire. The `ensure_*` pre-acquisitions remain necessary only because of this second flattening, yet the doc, `.claude/rules/auth.md:18` and five `state.rs` comments (558, 617, 627, 655, …) attribute it to a `String` boundary that was removed. `consent_required` is already asserted non-fatal (reauth.rs:263) and non-retryable, so passing it through is safe for fan-outs (bulk.rs:1190-1197 treats it as per-item).
proposal: Introduce `core::reauth::PASSTHROUGH_CODES = REAUTH_FATAL_CODES ∪ {"consent_required"}` (or make `passthrough_code` return `Some` for any non-empty classified `TokenError.code` and let `is_reauth_fatal` stay separate) so `GraphError/ArmError/ExchangeError/KeyVaultError::ui_code()` emit `consent_required`. Then rewrite the doc paragraph, `.claude/rules/auth.md`, and the `state.rs` comments to the true statement: the `ensure_*` probes exist to surface consent BEFORE side-effecting work and to bind a specific `consent_feature`, not because the boundary loses the code. Add a dto test: `UiError::from(GraphError::Token(TokenError::new("consent_required", ..))).code == "consent_required"`.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: http_error.rs macro `ui_code` passes only `reauth::passthrough_code` results (reauth.rs:47-49 = REAUTH_FATAL_CODES), so `GraphError::Token(TokenError{code:'consent_required'})` → `token_error`, while token_adapter.rs:25 does carry `consent_required`. Stronger than stated: there is no `ensure_write_token` (state.rs:587-678 lists arm/policy_write/sharepoint/group_member/audit_log/exchange/log_analytics only), so the default `consent_feature = "write"` fallback documented in auth-and-consent.md:73-80 and use_command.rs:100 cannot fire for the very case it describes (first Graph write in an un-consented tenant). Docs are stale in part: auth-and-consent.md:82-83, .claude/rules/auth.md and state.rs:589-590/:601 blame a `String` boundary that `TokenError{code}` replaced; state.rs:558/617/628/656 ('generic token_error') remain accurate. Passing `consent_required` through is safe: `is_retryable_code` (http_retry.rs:25-27) excludes it, reauth.rs:74 asserts it non-fatal, bulk.rs:1187-1200 treats it per-item.

title: Conditional Access tab ignores `conditions.clientApplications`, so workload-identity CA policies targeting the service principal are never shown
rationale: TOP-5 #3. Entra has two CA axes for an app: policies whose *target resource* is the app (`conditions.applications.includeApplications`) and Conditional Access for workload identities, where the *subject* is the service principal itself (`conditions.clientApplications.includeServicePrincipals` / `excludeServicePrincipals` / `servicePrincipalFilter`, gated on Workload Identities Premium). The model only deserializes `applications`, and `to_dto` returns `None` when it is absent, so a policy that blocks this SP from untrusted locations, or one that ties it to service-principal risk, renders as 'no policies apply'. For a tool whose subject matter is the service principal (Enterprise Applications, managed identities, the SP-only audit rows), the workload-identity axis is the one an admin hardening app identities cares about — and a tab that says nothing when a block policy exists actively misleads a troubleshooting session ('why does this app get AADSTS53003?'). The candidate list in the task ('Conditional Access for workload identities') is confirmed absent. The fetch already returns whole policy objects with no `$select` (directory.rs:78-95), so this is a model + classifier change with no new Graph call or scope.
proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (include/exclude SP ids + `servicePrincipalFilter {mode, rule}`) to `CaConditions`; extend `to_dto`/`applies_reason` to take the SP object id and emit distinct reason codes (`workloadIdentity`, `workloadIdentityFilter`) with exclude-wins semantics; add a target-axis field to `ConditionalAccessPolicyDto`; extend the existing `ConditionalAccessPanel` prop from `app_id` to `(app_id, sp_object_id)` so the already-mounted enterprise-pane instance (panels.rs:133) can pass the SP id; table tests mirroring `all_matches_unless_excluded`; README:130 wording.
verifier_notes: Model gap is real: `CaConditions` deserialises only `applications` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:612-617), `to_dto` returns None when it is absent (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/conditional_access.rs:56-61), and `applies_reason` only compares appIds (:79-110); no `clientApplications`/workload-identity handling anywhere (grep 0 hits). The fetch returns whole policy objects (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/directory.rs:78-95), so no new call/scope. HOWEVER the claim 'today it lives only on the app-registration pane' is false: `ConditionalAccessPanel` is already mounted on the enterprise pane at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/panels.rs:133 (import at mod.rs:36). What is missing there is that the panel takes only `app_id` (conditional_access_tab.rs:28), so the SP object id needed for the workload-identity axis is not passed. Tests to mirror exist (`all_matches_unless_excluded`, conditional_access.rs:176). Workload-identity CA is Workload Identities Premium-gated, which tempers the reach.

title: Inner $batch 5xx sub-responses are terminal while the same GET alone is retried — one transient 503 sub-response marks the whole site sweep incomplete/uncached and strands a DR backup object
rationale: The single-request transport retries every 5xx (transport.rs:613-651: anything not 4xx falls to `Attempt::Retry`), but inside a batch a 502/503/504 on one sub-request is mapped straight to `Server` and never re-batched. So the same object read has two retry policies depending on whether it travelled batched or alone — for the DR backup that means a transient 503 on one sub-request becomes a permanently 'skipped' object in the backup manifest, and for the audit prewarm a cold lean-SP entry. Microsoft's throttling guidance for batching says to retry each failed request from the batch individually; the machinery (`pending`/`throttled` index list + `RetryBudget`) is already there for 429.
proposal: Extend the re-batch predicate at batch.rs:281 to `matches!(sub.status, 429 | 502 | 503 | 504) && budget.may_retry()`, notifying the throttle observer for 429 only; `budget.wait(max_retry_after)` already falls back to jittered exponential backoff when no inner Retry-After exists (core/http_retry.rs:265-269), so no new backoff code is needed. Add a wiremock test mirroring `batch_get_json_retries_inner_429_then_surfaces_throttled` with an inner 503 that succeeds on the second POST, and one where an inner 503 that exhausts the budget still surfaces as `Server`.
verifier_notes: Core premise verified: batch.rs:279-289 re-batches only `sub.status == 429`; :72-74 maps 5xx straight to `GraphError::Server`; the single-request path retries every non-4xx (transport.rs:612-621 `_ => None` → `Attempt::Retry`). Two parts are overstated or stale: (1) the cited Microsoft guidance (learn.microsoft.com/graph/throttling#throttling-and-batching) says to retry each *throttled* (429) request from a batch individually — it does not speak to 5xx sub-responses; (2) the 'audit prewarm cold lean-SP entry' example is stale — the batched lean prewarm was replaced by the SP index scan (commands/audit.rs:190-199). The real consumers are the DR backup, where a `Server` sub-error becomes a recorded `SkippedObject` (commands/backup.rs:397-441, 811) — honest, but a re-run is needed — and, unmentioned by the reviewer, the site sweep, where `batch_list_site_permissions` (sharepoint.rs:45-63) sub-errors are folded into `sites_failed`, which makes the whole 5000-site sweep incomplete and uncached (commands/sharepoint.rs:975-992). Enhancement, not a correctness bug, since both paths degrade honestly; medium is defensible because of the sweep cost.

title: Scoped writes (group membership, site/list/item grants, claims policies) bypass the retry loop entirely, so a 429 with Retry-After fails immediately where the identical unscoped write would be replayed
rationale: The 'one-shot configuration write' rationale no longer holds: `add_group_member` is called from the DR restore loop over every restored SP, and `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission`/`grant_site_permission` run inside the multi-target grant loop. `RetryReason::Throttled` is explicitly documented in http_retry.rs as safe to replay for any verb ('the service rejected the request before doing any work'), and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider plus `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` — the scoped GET family (`scoped_get_retried`) already made this move. Today a write that rides `write_token` gets its 429 honored exactly per Retry-After; the same PATCH/POST on `sharepoint_token` or `group_member_token` fails on the first 429 and the restore/grant loop records a failure the operator has to redo. AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule for the retry budget is what this violates.
proposal: Reimplement `scoped_send_core` on `send_core_url_with(token, retry_class_for(&method), method, url, &[], false, body_value, None)` — derive the class from the verb (as `send_core_url` does at transport.rs:449-461 and as the `repo_invariants/trust.rs:135` invariant expects) rather than hardcoding `RetryClass::NonIdempotent`, so scoped DELETEs (`remove_site_permission`, `remove_list_permission`, `remove_group_member`, claims-policy unassign) stay idempotent-replayable while POST/PATCH are replayed only after a 429. Update the doc comments at transport.rs:78-82 and the sharepoint/policies callers' expectations; keep `scoped_get` one-shot (pinned by tests/transport.rs:306). Add the two wiremock tests as proposed (429 Retry-After:0 then 201 succeeds; 502 on a scoped POST hits `.expect(1)`).
verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:120-155 `scoped_send_core` does a single `req.send()` and maps the status with `map_error_status`; the rationale at :78-82 ('one-shot configuration writes, not high-volume reads') predates the loops that now call it: `add_group_member` (directory.rs:216-224) is invoked per restored SP in commands/restore.rs:709-716; `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission` (sharepoint.rs:475-516, both `scoped_send_json`) run inside the dedupe_targets loop at commands/sharepoint.rs:566-600 (added in cf32c3d, 2026-08-28). core/http_retry.rs:113-114 documents `Throttled` as safe to replay for any verb, and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider + class (transport.rs:472-482). The only test pinning one-shot behaviour is for the scoped GET (`list_synchronization_jobs`, tests/transport.rs:306-333), not the write family, so no pinned decision is contradicted. Rides the AGENTS.md 'one definition per policy' rule: these writes bypass `core::http_retry` entirely and never notify the throttle observer. One refinement to the proposal: hardcoding NonIdempotent would downgrade the scoped DELETEs that today would be Idempotent under `retry_class_for`.

Severity lowered from medium: it is a latent fragility, not a present defect, and the trigger (someone trimming the updater's defaults or a plugin default change) is speculative; the value is that the regression would be invisible to CI.

title: During the tenant-wide prefetch the audit progress block reads '0 / 0 apps' with no phase label
rationale: The inline comment at :160-166 says the prefetch 'is the longest phase of a large run' and 'the most likely moment for an operator to press Cancel'. `security_view.rs:180-183` renders the progress block only once `progress` is `Some`, so for that entire phase the operator sees a disabled button with a tiny spinner and a Cancel button, with no indication of what is happening or that the app is alive. title: Adopt servicePrincipalRiskDetections (v1.0) to flag risky workload identities in the audit
rationale: A least-privilege audit that scores every SP but is blind to Entra's own "leaked credentials" or "malicious application" detections misses the highest-signal finding available; the endpoint is GA in v1.0 and follows the same optional-scope, graceful-degradation pattern as the CA and audit-log tokens.
proposal: Add an on-demand `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All` token (`consent_scopes_for("risk")`) with a catalog row, fetch detections once per audit run (cache like the SP sign-in report), join on `servicePrincipalId`, and add a top-severity finding "Entra ID Protection flags this workload identity (riskEventType)" that is never cached when the read fails.

title: Terminal bulk-progress events report done == total even for a cancelled or halted run (a documented contract with a one-frame UI effect); the credential sweep emits no terminal event
rationale: After a Cancel at item 3 of 10, or a dead-session halt, the final event tells the UI '10 / 10 (cancelled)'. `BulkProgressRow` (bulk_action_bar.rs:227) renders `p.done / p.total`, so the bar snaps to 100% for a run that processed a fraction of the selection — the same 'partial reads as complete' shape the surrounding code is careful about elsewhere. `bulk_remove_expired_credentials` emits no terminal event at all, so the three fan-out paths and the sequential driver disagree on the contract.
proposal: If harmonising: emit `done: outcomes.len()` (sequential) / collected count (fan-outs) as the terminal value, update run_bulk_seq's doc and `a_cancel_before_the_first_item_processes_nothing` (which currently pins `(1, None)`), and add a matching terminal event to bulk_remove_expired_credentials. Otherwise leave as-is and only add the missing terminal event to the sweep for contract consistency.
verifier_notes: The events are as quoted: bulk.rs:1014-1020 (run_bulk_seq), :379-386 (bulk_delete_applications) and :497-504 (bulk_grant_permissions) all emit `done: total` regardless of cancellation, and bulk_remove_expired_credentials (:140-297) emits no terminal event at all. But this is a documented and tested contract, not an oversight: run_bulk_seq's doc (:970-971) states 'then a final `done = total` event', and `a_cancel_before_the_first_item_processes_nothing` (:1120-1133) asserts the terminal `(1, None)` with `cancelled == true` for a run that processed nothing. UI impact is negligible: `BulkProgressRow` is mounted only while `busy` (bulk_action_bar.rs:646-647, doc at :198-200) and the command returns immediately after the terminal emit, so the '100%' state is at most one frame; the bar also clears `progress` at the next run start for exactly this reason (:495-497). title: Switching tenants requires a relaunch by design (single-tenant-bound instance is a documented invariant); ergonomics of the switch could be improved without breaking it
rationale: The 0.30.0 CHANGELOG itself names the persona: 'a consultant working several tenants had to re-point the app from outside the UI', and the fix was a Settings tab that saves the pair and relaunches. Everything below the auth service is already multi-tenant by construction — `graph_for(&tenant_id)`/`exchange_clients` are per-tenant maps, every cache key is `{tenant_id}|…`, `TenantScopedUi::reset()` and the open-items dock are keyed by tenant, and `tenant_defaults` in `settings.json` is a `BTreeMap<tenant_id, TenantDefaults>` — so the only single-tenant components are `UserSettings.{client_id,tenant_id}`, `AppState::new` resolving them once (state.rs:235-260), and `EntraAuthService::new(client_id, tenant_id)`. An MSP or multi-region admin switching between three tenants several times a day pays a full process restart, a browser round trip, and loses the audit run each time. This is the 'multi-tenant quick switch' item, verified absent.
proposal: Keep one tenant per process. Cheaper, invariant-preserving form: store several saved profiles (`label, client_id, tenant_id`) in settings.json alongside the existing pair, add a 'Switch tenant…' picker in the account menu that saves the chosen pair and relaunches (reusing `set_auth_config` + `restart_app`), and preserve the last audit export path. If the maintainers want in-process switching, open a design issue that explicitly revisits backup-and-restore.md:10-13 first.
verifier_notes: Premise true: `set_auth_config` persists one pair and requires a relaunch (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/config.rs:27-33), `UserSettings` holds one client_id/tenant_id (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:27-31), `AppState::new` resolves them once (state.rs:232-257), and `sign_in` rejects a foreign `tid` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:313-318); CHANGELOG.md:44-45 names the consultant persona. BUT this is a documented, deliberate invariant the reviewer did not engage with: docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:10-13 — 'A running instance therefore can **never** touch two tenants. We do not change that. … This preserves the single-tenant security invariant and needs no multi-authority auth.' The whole DR shape ('file-bridged, two single-tenant instances') is built on it, and the repo's #1 footgun (cross-tenant cache leakage) is what the invariant defends. A proposal to make the auth service multi-authority overturns an architecture decision and must be raised as such, not shipped as an L feature. Frontend `set_active_tenant` (web-rs/src/state/tenant.rs:18) exists but is only ever fed one tenant per process.

title: apply_exchange_mailbox_scope's warnings name each failed strip/assignment but never summarize which permissions remain org-wide, unlike migrate_one
rationale: When the operator asked for the strip but a role assignment failed, or the assignments list could not be read, the result still carries scope_name/scope_filter and the UI shows "N roles assigned, M grants removed". title: No cleanup path for an app's orphaned management scope / SP pointer / managed group after decommissioning
rationale: An operator who removes an app's scoped Exchange access (or decommissions the app) is left with an orphaned `app_scope_<appId>` scope, an SP pointer and a managed group. Because `ensure_management_scope` is create-only by design, re-granting later with a different group set hits the `scope_group_mismatch` refusal (grants.rs:245-258) until someone deletes the stale scope by hand in PowerShell - the one thing this toolkit exists to replace. The crate already has the enumeration primitives (`get_role_assignments`, `list_management_scopes`, `references_to_group`) needed to prove the scope is unreferenced before deleting it.
proposal: Optional feature: an opt-in, separately confirmed teardown (proving zero Get-ManagementRoleAssignment rows reference the scope and zero assignments remain for the pointer) modelled on delete_exchange_scope_group's live re-checks. Do not present it as unblocking re-grants — that path already exists via 'Move to managed group'.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: no Remove-ManagementScope/Remove-ServicePrincipal anywhere; grants.rs:471-473 pushes the 'left in place' warning; ensure_management_scope is create-only (rbac.rs:75-77). But leaving them is a deliberate, user-facing decision — the frontend copy at exchange_scoping_section.rs:614 says the scope and group are 'left in place so the scoping can be re-applied'. The central claim that a later re-grant with a different group set is blocked 'until someone deletes the stale scope by hand in PowerShell' is wrong: the scope_group_mismatch message (grants.rs:245-258) directs to 'Move to managed group', and move_exchange_scope_to_managed_group (scope_group.rs:685+) repoints the scope via set_management_scope_filter inside the toolkit. What remains is an orphan-cleanup gap on decommissioning, which is a feature request, not a medium bug.

title: CSV exports are written without a UTF-8 BOM; non-ASCII display names open garbled in Excel on Windows
rationale: Excel (the README's implied consumer for CSV) sniffs encoding by BOM; without one it decodes UTF-8 as the ANSI code page, so `Zürich Finanz` or a Japanese app name renders as mojibake. The formula-injection guard shows this code already targets Excel. `#`-comment-block readers (`pandas`, R) accept a BOM with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`.
proposal: In `save_export_via_dialog`'s `"csv"` arm and in `save_csv_via_dialog`, prefix the content with `\u{FEFF}` (one place: a `fn csv_bytes(s: String) -> Vec<u8>` used by both). Add a test that the first three bytes are `EF BB BF` and that `csv_columns` on the header line is unaffected. Effort S.
verifier_notes: Verified: `write_via_dialog` (export.rs:113-128) writes `content.into_bytes()` raw and is the single sink for every CSV — both `save_export_via_dialog`'s csv arm (:46-60) and `save_csv_via_dialog` (:141-154) route through it; repo grep for FEFF/BOM in apps/ and crates/ finds nothing. The formula-injection guard at export.rs:12-13 explicitly names Excel/Sheets as the consumer, so Excel's ANSI fallback for BOM-less UTF-8 is a legitimate concern for non-ASCII display names. One trade-off worth documenting in the fix: the `#` comment-block convention (export.rs:157-165) targets pandas/R readers; pandas strips a UTF-8 BOM automatically but base R `read.csv` needs `fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM"`. Low, S effort, one choke point.

title: Key Vault rotation writes secret versions with no ownership tags and no collision check
rationale: `set_secret` on an existing name silently appends a version. Nothing in the written version records which app registration, object id or `keyId` it belongs to, so (1) a typo or a shared secret name across two apps overwrites another app's live secret with no warning — consumers of the old value break at their next read — and (2) an operator auditing the vault later cannot tell which app a version was minted for. The tool already knows all three identifiers at this point and already persists the vault→app binding in `UserSettings`, so the information exists; it just is not written where the vault reader can see it.
proposal: Populate `SecretSetRequest.tags` (`azapptoolkit-app-id`, `azapptoolkit-object-id`, `azapptoolkit-key-id`) and `content_type` in `rotate_app_credential` (keyvault.rs:117-122) via a pure, unit-tested builder. For the ownership check, do not call `get_secret` (it returns the secret value just to read tags); add a metadata-only `list_secret_versions(name)` (`GET /secrets/{name}/versions`, returns attributes + tags) to crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs and compare the latest version's `azapptoolkit-app-id` tag. Return `UiError::validation("secret_owned_by_other_app", …)` on mismatch; defer a `force` override until the rotation dialog grows a control for it (RotateCredentialInput has no such field today).
verifier_notes: Premise real: keyvault.rs:117-122 sets `tags: None, content_type: None`; `SecretSetRequest` supports both (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:72-80); the vault→app binding is persisted only in UserSettings (keyvault.rs:155-175), invisible to a vault reader. Proposal adjustments: the KV client exposes only `list_secrets`/`get_secret`/`set_secret` (client.rs:72-102), so the collision check needs a new metadata-only versions call rather than reading the live value, and `input.force` does not exist in `RotateCredentialInput` (dto/keyvault.rs:125-138). Severity downgraded to low: it is an enhancement; the hazard requires an operator to type another app's secret name, and tagging alone is cheap and safe.

title: Office 365 SharePoint Online is the documented seam: the tester ignores org-wide Sites.* grants on that resource and the converter can't strip them
rationale: The converter limitation is a documented, gated decision and is not re-litigated here. But the read-only tester has no such gate: an app holding Sites.FullControl.All on Office 365 SharePoint Online (SharePoint REST/CSOM) reaches every site, yet sharepoint_grants_held never sees that resource, so path 1 is skipped and the app can read as no_access. Widening the tester is safe and is the first half of the seam the core docs describe; the converter is the second.

Nothing in test_site_access's doc (:1037-1041, 'An org-wide Sites.* … app-role grant reaches every resource') or sharepoint-selected.md describes the tester as Graph-only by design, so the read-only widening is a legitimate first half of the documented seam. Implementation note: mirror prefetch_ews_full_access_grants (audit.rs:1015-1021) — a tenant with no SPO-consenting app has no SP for that resource, which must read as an ordinary empty set, not a failure. Step 2 (converter strips SPO grants, gate widens, CHANGELOG note) is correctly scoped as M with a ranking-shift note per AGENTS.md.

But 'Missing' currently conflates two states with different remedies: eligible (go activate, 2 minutes) versus not assigned at all (file a request with the PIM owner, days). title: Claims-mapping (Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration) and provisioning read (Synchronization.Read.All) have no capabilities-catalog entry, so readiness never lists them and SSO 403s carry no role remediation

title: Restore dry-run omits the schema-too-new blocker and the Pass 4/5 counts, so a too-new manifest is rejected only after the confirm click
rationale: `plan_restore` is documented as the operator's chance to inspect before writes (backup-and-restore.md "The frontend shows it before the operator confirms"). The cloud-mismatch blocker is computed there, but the newer-schema refusal is not, so the operator loads the file, reads a plausible plan, confirms the modal, and only then gets `schema_too_new`. Severity is overstated: the schema check fires before any write, so the cost is a wasted confirm click and a late error message, not a partial restore. Enhancement, low.

title: Search corpus reports SP-index truncation but discards the app-registration index's own truncation
rationale: `app_name_index_cached` is capped at `APPS_MAX` (10 000) too. A tenant with more registrations than service principals (automation-heavy tenants accumulate registrations without SPs) has its app-reg half truncated while `corpus_truncated` stays false, so the dropdown says "No matches" for a registration that exists; the doc calls both caps "must not drift" and the SP one is already surfaced for exactly this reason.
proposal: Compute `index_truncated: sps.len() >= SP_INDEX_MAX || apps.len() >= APPS_MAX` (rename the field; the DTO field `corpus_truncated` already abstracts the source), or return the `truncated` bool from `list_application_index_named` and carry it through `app_name_index_cached`.

title: GUID search swallows probe failures, so a throttled or dead-session lookup renders as "No matches"
rationale: The module's own contract is that search must never silently omit. On the GUID path a 429, a 403 (operator without SP read), or a dead token on all four probes is indistinguishable from a genuine 404, and the frontend has no signal to show, so an admin pasting an appId from the portal concludes the app does not exist. `Err(GraphError::NotFound)` is the only error that means "not there".
proposal: Distinguish `Err(GraphError::NotFound(_))` (a real miss) from other errors in the GUID branch; add `#[serde(default)] pub lookup_degraded: bool` to `GlobalSearchResults` (additive, like the five existing defaults) set when any probe failed with a non-404, and render it through the same `cap_notice` slot ("Directory lookup failed; results may be incomplete"). Unit-test `assemble_guid_hits` with an `Err(Throttled)` input.
verifier_notes: search.rs:263-276: all four probes are collapsed with `.ok()`/`.ok().flatten()`; only `get_application` (via `GraphError::NotFound`, http_error.rs:74) and the `Ok(None)` forms mean 'not there' (service_principals.rs:528-535 maps 404 to None), so a 429 past the retry budget or a 403 is indistinguishable from a miss, and search.rs:289 hardcodes `corpus_truncated: false`; global_search.rs:319 renders a notice only from that flag. The module doc (search.rs:12-16) states the contract the branch violates. The additive `#[serde(default)]` pattern already exists on GlobalSearchResults (dto/search.rs:34-40). Severity lowered to low: the result is per-query (not cached), the HTTP layer already retries throttling, and a dead token would fail every other surface too; still a genuine, cheap contract fix.

title: with_replication_retry skips steps 4 and 5 of the SAML create flow
rationale: Steps 2, 3 and 5b are wrapped against the post-instantiate replication 404, but the two writes between them — the certificate POST and the activation PATCH, both against the same freshly created SP — are not. Graph front-doors are not sticky, so a request routed to a lagging replica at step 4 fails with NotFound and leaves the half-configured app the retry exists to prevent, while the cheaper best-effort step right after it would have retried.
proposal: Wrap both: `with_replication_retry(|| client.add_token_signing_certificate(sp_id, &subject, end)).await?` and the step-5 PATCH. Both closures are `FnMut() -> Fut` over borrowed data, so no restructuring is needed.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. sso/mod.rs:207-236: steps 2, 3 (and 5b at :240-241) are wrapped in `with_replication_retry`, while `add_token_signing_certificate` (:221-223) and the activation PATCH (:226-234) against the same fresh SP are not; the module doc (:12-14) states the PATCH steps after instantiate are wrapped, so the omission reads as an oversight, not a decision. Both closures are feasible as `FnMut() -> Fut` over borrowed data (`end` is `Copy`, `subject` borrowed; build the patch body once). Retrying a POST on NotFound is safe because NotFound means nothing was created. Mitigating: step 2 has already succeeded against the SP by step 4, so the window is narrower than for step 2 itself — low is right.

title: Saved views snapshot only facet + search; the drawer's date range is neither saved nor cleared on apply
rationale: The drawer presents saved views and the created-on range as one filter set, but 'Save view' captures only two of the three inputs. A view like 'Disabled, created this quarter' cannot be saved, and applying any saved view leaves whatever date range is currently set still active — the `FilterToggle` badge keeps counting it — so the applied view shows fewer rows than when it was saved with no visible reason.
proposal: Extend `SavedView` with `#[serde(default)] after: Option<NaiveDate>, before: Option<NaiveDate>` (backward-compatible with existing localStorage payloads), thread the two range signals from `ListScaffold` into `SavedViews`, write them on save and set them (including to `None`) on apply.

So a saved view cannot capture a date range and applying one leaves the current range active. Proposal (`#[serde(default)]` optional dates threaded from `ListScaffold`, set including to `None` on apply) is backward-compatible with stored payloads and feasible; the MI list has no date range and would pass nothing.

title: Authentication form has no Reset or dirty state; Overview Save round-trips an empty PATCH (and busts list caches) when nothing changed

<div class="actions-row">

title: Pre-authorized client add is a GUID-only field with no directory lookup, and existing rows show the bare GUID with no display name
rationale: Pre-authorizing a client skips user consent, so a mistyped or wrong GUID is a security-relevant error that today only surfaces as a Graph 400 (or silently pre-authorizes the wrong app if the GUID happens to exist). The frontend already has a tenant SP index and a `list_app_role_resources`-style picker group ("Tenant app registrations") that resolve name + appId; the row also renders the raw GUID with no display name (line 567), so the operator cannot tell which app is authorized.
proposal: Add a typeahead over the tenant's app registrations/service principals (appId + display name — the SP index / `list_app_role_resources`-style catalog already resolves these) for the add path, and resolve display names for existing `pre_authorized_applications` rows from the SP index (falling back to the GUID). Client-side GUID-shape validation is optional polish since the backend already returns a validation error before Graph.

What holds: the add path is a free-text `` (expose_api_tab.rs:741-746) with no typeahead over the tenant's app registrations, existing rows render the bare GUID (:567 `{p.app_id}`) with no display name, and a *well-formed but wrong* GUID is indeed only caught by Graph (or not at all if it exists). A feature request, low severity.

title: Observed-activity panel promises a 'GETs-only → Downgrade' verdict but renders raw rows with no method roll-up (a gate-safe partial of #110)
rationale: Issue #110 is correctly gated: mapping `(method, path-family) → permission-family` without live data risks a confidently wrong 'safe to downgrade'. But the method axis alone is not guesswork — a KQL `summarize` by `RequestMethod` is a fact, and the panel's own header text promises exactly the 'only GETs observed' reading while leaving the operator to eyeball up to 200 rows. Surfacing 'N calls: 100% GET, 0 write methods observed over 90 days (long tail truncated)' is a factual hint that stays inside the gate (no path buckets, no permission verdict), and it is the observation that makes `downgrade_application_permission` (already a command) worth clicking. It should be labelled as an observation, not a verdict, to honour the issue's reasoning.
proposal: (S) Add `method_totals: Vec<(String, u64)>` to `GraphUsageResult` (computed from the rows, or a second cheap `summarize by RequestMethod` in the same query) and render a one-line roll-up above the table: 'Write methods observed: none' / 'POST 12, PATCH 3, DELETE 1' with a `Callout tone=info` that explicitly says this is not a permission verdict and links to the Downgrade action only when zero non-GET calls were seen AND `truncated == false`. One nuance the reviewer already handles: rows are capped by `USAGE_ROW_CAP`, so a roll-up computed from rows is incomplete when `truncated` — the 'only when truncated == false' gate (or a second `summarize by RequestMethod` in the same query) is required, as proposed.

title: `KeyVaultResource` drops `properties.enableRbacAuthorization`, so the RBAC sweep cannot tell a legacy access-policy vault from one with no assignments — the UI admits both "produce no rows"
rationale: The ARM vault list already returns `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` on every item; discarding it means the sweep's coverage numbers (`vaults_scanned`) count access-policy vaults as scanned-and-empty, when in fact their access model is invisible to `roleAssignments`. For a security posture surface that is a silent gap: an operator sees 40 scanned vaults and 12 with rows and cannot tell which of the other 28 are governed by access policies (a finding in itself — AGENTS/capabilities treat legacy mode as a problem).
proposal: Add `properties: Option<KeyVaultResourceProperties { enable_rbac_authorization: Option<bool> }>` to `KeyVaultResource`; in `sweep_key_vault_access` skip the roleAssignments read for `false` vaults, count them in a new `vaults_access_policy_mode` field on `KeyVaultSweepResult`, and show it beside `vaults_failed` in the panel (optionally as a Security-tab finding "vault uses legacy access policies"). Wiremock test for the property.
verifier_notes: crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/models.rs:97-108 `KeyVaultResource` deserializes only `id`/`name`; the ARM vault list (`Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults` at subscription scope) returns full `Vault` objects whose `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` is available. `sweep_key_vault_access` (keyvault_rbac.rs:150-200) counts every vault as `vaults_scanned` and the DTO (dto/keyvault.rs:40-49) has no access-policy-mode counter. Two corrections to the framing: (1) the gap is not silent — the UI empty-state at web-rs views/resource_access/keyvault.rs:354 explicitly names legacy access-policy vaults as a known limitation, and core capabilities.rs:326 already warns about RBAC mode; (2) RBAC role assignments are control-plane objects that exist regardless of the vault's permission model, so an access-policy vault with a direct assignment WILL produce rows — the flag is needed to annotate that those rows do not confer data-plane access, not merely to explain empties. Useful enhancement for a posture surface; low severity.

title: Browser launch failure is only logged; the authorize URL is never surfaced, so the operator waits out the full 300 s with no way to proceed

On a desktop with no default browser handler, a snap/flatpak-confined `xdg-open`, or a Windows policy that blocks the handler, sign-in silently hangs until the 300 s timeout and then shows a network hint. grep of web-rs finds no "copy link"/manual-open affordance.

title: No visibility of tenant app-management policies (credential lifetime / type enforcement); audit and Credentials tab cannot explain a policy-rejected secret add
rationale: TOP-5 #5. Entra's app management policies (`/policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy`, `/policies/appManagementPolicies`, `/applications/{id}/appManagementPolicies`) are the tenant control that *prevents* the findings this audit reports after the fact: `passwordAddition` blocks new client secrets, `passwordLifetime`/`symmetricKeyLifetime` cap durations, `customPasswordAddition` blocks portal-set secrets, `keyCredential` restrictions require asymmetric keys, `nonDefaultUriAddition` blocks URI hijack. The audit's Rules 7 and 17 ('Long-lived secrets (>1 year)', 'Uses client secret(s)') and the per-app Credentials tab give no hint whether the tenant already enforces a policy, whether this app is exempted by a custom policy, or why an `add_password` just failed with a policy violation. The read scope is `Policy.Read.All` (the existing `policy` feature; the same scope already gates the CA tab) and the write scope is `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` (the existing `policy_write` feature used for claims mapping), so no new consent surface is needed. For an admin managing apps at scale this is the difference between remediating each app and turning the tap off once.
proposal: Phase 1 (M, read-only) as proposed for the three `GraphClient` reads and a best-effort `TenantAppPolicyDto` in the audit prefetch — but keep `LONG_LIVED_SECRET_DAYS` as the legacy floor and add the effective `passwordLifetime` as an *additional* advisory comparison (with a CHANGELOG entry), plus the Credentials-tab `Callout` and a Home posture line. Add the `capabilities.rs` entry. Phase 2 (writes) as proposed behind `policy_write`.

But the framing 'audit hardcodes a 365-day threshold' presents a deliberate legacy port as a defect: `LONG_LIVED_SECRET_DAYS` cites `Credential-Analysis.ps1:169` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/permissions.rs:28-29), and AGENTS.md requires scoring rules to cite the PowerShell origin. Replacing the constant with a policy-derived value is a ranking change (CHANGELOG-gated) and must not silently remove the legacy floor. title: mutate's process-wide lock does not cover a second app instance; std's File::lock (stable since 1.89, MSRV 1.98) would close the gap without a dependency
rationale: The lost-update race `mutate` fixes reappears across processes: two windows/instances (nothing prevents launching a second) each read-modify-write settings.json; the atomic rename means the file is never torn, but the second writer's snapshot silently drops the first's field (e.g. a vault binding recorded by a rotation in one instance is overwritten by a defaults save in the other). Since MSRV is 1.98, `std::fs::File::lock`/`try_lock` (stabilised in 1.89) gives a cross-process advisory lock with no new crate.
proposal: In `mutate`, after taking `SETTINGS_LOCK`, open (create) `<config_dir>/settings.lock` and call `.lock()?` on it for the duration of the read-modify-write; the guard drops with the `File`. This composes with the atomic rename and keeps `stored()` lock-free for readers. Alternatively adopt `tauri-plugin-single-instance`, but that is a dependency and a broader behaviour change.
verifier_notes: settings.rs:116-120 shows a process-wide `static Mutex`, so two processes can interleave `stored()`/`save_locked()`. No single-instance plugin is registered (lib.rs:24-25 has only updater + dialog; grep for `single_instance`/`File::lock`/`fs2`/`fd-lock` finds nothing), so a second instance is possible on Windows (the primary target) and Linux. rust-toolchain.toml:5 pins 1.98.1, above the 1.89 stabilisation of `File::lock`/`try_lock`/`unlock`, so an advisory lock on `<config_dir>/settings.lock` needs no new dependency and composes with the atomic rename in private_file. The race requires two instances writing within milliseconds of each other, which is rare in practice — low/enhancement is honest. Note `File::lock` releases when the `File` is dropped (or `unlock()`), so holding the `File` for the read-modify-write scope is sufficient; keep it inside the existing `SETTINGS_LOCK` so in-process callers still serialise without contending on the OS lock.

title: remove_key_credential / remove_service_principal_key_credential PATCH the unchanged array and report success when the key id is absent — and the remediation counts it as a removal
rationale: Both fetch-modify-PATCH removers write the full collection back even when nothing matched `key_id` (another admin already removed it, or the audit's cached finding is stale). The write is a no-op on Graph but the caller sees `Ok(())`, so the audit's one-click 'remove expired credentials' Fix and bulk remove report a removal that did not happen, and the command layer then busts `apps_pairing`/detail/audit caches for nothing. `remove_password` (the `removePassword` action) gets a real 404 from Graph in the same situation, so the two credential kinds behave differently.
proposal: In both removers, detect an empty match (compare lengths, or `find` the entry first) and return `Err(GraphError::NotFound(format!("keyCredential {key_id}")))` without sending the PATCH. Then adjust the callers, because none of them currently handles NotFound as 'already gone': `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (commands/remediation.rs:69-79) should treat NotFound from either `remove_password` or `remove_key_credential` as already-removed (skip, do not increment `removed_*`, do not abort the loop) rather than surfacing it as a failure; `remove_certificate_credential` (commands/applications/credentials.rs:236-247) and the SSO retire path (commands/sso/mod.rs:960-963) can let NotFound propagate. Add the wiremock test asserting no PATCH is sent for an unknown key id.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: credentials.rs:198-209 filters `live_key_credentials` by `keyId` and PATCHes whatever remains, returning `Ok(())` even when nothing matched; credentials.rs:251-300 (`remove_service_principal_key_credential`) has the same shape (with a `thumbprint` of `None` the filter is a no-op and the PATCH is still sent). The remediation at commands/remediation.rs:77-82 then increments `removed_certificates` and busts caches via `invalidate_app_credentials` (:91-93). What is overstated: the reviewer says 'Callers already map NotFound for the password path' — they do not; remediation.rs:69-73 breaks and returns the error on any `remove_password` failure, and there is no 'already gone' handling anywhere on these paths (grep for NotFound/already in remediation.rs and applications/credentials.rs returns nothing). So the proposal as written would turn a concurrently-removed certificate from a silently-counted success into a hard remediation failure; the caller change above is needed for the fix to be an improvement. The `remove_password` 404 claim is plausible (Graph's `removePassword` action rejects an unknown keyId) but is not something the repo pins. Low is right.

If this is a secret backing a certificate, then managed will be true'). models.rs:6-16 omits it and commands/keyvault.rs:35-48 maps only name/id/enabled/expires/content_type — premise holds for the browser. title: `verify`'s closing summary omits `web-itest-size` from the gates it did not run
rationale: The size gate is `cargo test --no-run` for wasm32 plus `wc -c` — it needs neither Chrome nor network, yet only `verify-full` runs it, and `verify`'s closing message lists only the network gates as "NOT run", so a contributor reasonably believes `verify` covers everything a browserless box can check. A shard drifting past 52 MB is exactly the CI-only, opaque-timeout failure the recipe was written to pre-empt (justfile:131-139).

Optionally run `web-itest-size` from the `[unix]` `web-itest-auto` only AFTER a successful `web-itest`, where the shard objects are hot and the recipe is a relink (justfile:155-156). Do not add it to the skip path: without a prior `web-itest`, `cargo test --no-run --target wasm32 --features test-support` is a full ~45-50 s codegen build of four shards (justfile:22-25) on top of `web-clippy`'s check-only pass.

Low severity: the honest summary line is the genuine fix.
